John — thanks for the redline and the quick timeline. Attaching a concise counter-proposal (RIA_MSA_counter_v2.docx) — highlights below.

Quick options for Acme (commercial tradeoffs noted):

1) Rolling 12-month ceiling (our preferred):
   - Liability limited to the greater of (i) $500k or (ii) 3x the fees paid in the 12 months preceding the claim.
   - Pros: aligns with run-rate, caps exposure for high-growth customers.
   - Commercial: no price uplift for this structure; requires standard security attestation.

2) Aggregate contract-term ceiling (conservative for supplier):
   - Liability capped at 2x total fees paid under the Agreement (all-time aggregate).
   - Pros: simpler for procurement to reason about at signature.
   - Commercial: for multi-year commits we would require a 7–10% uplift or a small non-refundable commit (we can model).
   
3) Hybrid (middle ground):
   - Per-incident cap = 1x monthly fee up to a maximum annual cap of 4x trailing 12-month fees.
   - Pros: protects both parties; more complexity in billing reconciliation.

Carveouts we will accept: IP indemnity (subject to standard final language), will exclude consequential damages from recoverable damages, and retain a separate carveout for willful misconduct/gross negligence (survival language). For data breaches we prefer an explicit remediation-and-credit approach vs unlimited monetary exposure.

Ask: Laura — can you confirm redline language for the rolling-window option and any minimum dollar floors we should use for enterprise vs mid-market?

John — if you can tell us which of the three options Acme prefers, we'll return a tracked MSA with the exact clause language and a one-line commercial uplift estimate if required.

Matt/Maria — quick legal take below (rolled into RIA_MSA_counter_v2). I lean to the Rolling 12-month ceiling (Option 1) with a modest floor for smaller customers. Rationale and drafting notes: 

- Why rolling 12-month: it ties exposure to current spend. For SaaS/usage contracts this avoids windfall exposures where early-term fees are low but tail usage spikes.
- Floor & multiple: propose language: "Total liability for all causes shall not exceed the greater of (a) $500,000 or (b) three (3) times the Fees paid by Customer in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim." For enterprise customers we can make the floor negotiable (e.g., $1M).
- Carveouts (we should keep these): IP indemnity (separate indemnity obligations), willful misconduct/gross negligence (survival), and breach of confidentiality (we currently limit damages but should keep remediation obligations). Note: we avoid unlimited monetary liability for data breaches; instead propose specific data-breach caps tied to the same formula and an obligation to remediate + credit.
- Consequential damages: accept exclusion as requested — keep definition aligned to typical commercial language.

Commercial impact: 3x rolling with $500k floor is our standard for mid-market and up. If Acme insists on higher multiple or higher floor we should ask for either: (i) a price uplift (suggest 8–12% ARR uplift), or (ii) a limited escrow / letter of credit for critical deployments.

Next steps: Mateo — if you confirm Acme is ok with Option 1 in principle, I'll prepare a tracked MSA clause and mark the commercial uplift scenarios for the pricing team. If they instead want Aggregate-term (Option 2), we need to price uplift immediately.
